page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6a.4xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7H12 processor operating at a base clock speed of 2.6 GHz. It features 16 virtual CPUs corresponding to 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled, along with 64.0 GB of memory. This provides a balanced vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 1:4. The instance runs under KVM hypervisor virtualization and includes a 5 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile. Local NVMe SSD storage is not included, and there are no attached hardware acceleration GPUs.

Performance benchmark evaluations place the ecs.g6a.4xlarge in the average tier for multi-threaded processing and application execution. Key metrics include a Geekbench multi-core score of 7328, a PassMark CPU score of 19093.04, and a software compilation score of 13291. Key application metrics show static web serving throughput reaching 6.8 GB/sec and Redis SET performance measuring 14.17 million operations per second. Hardware tradeoffs include lower single-core compute performance, as shown by a stress-ng single-core score of 767.49, as well as reduced uncached memory bandwidth measuring 30.52 GB/sec for reads and 15.5 GB/sec for writes.

Given its balanced resource configuration without attached disk or accelerator overhead, the instance delivers qualitative cost efficiency for generalized compute tasks that rely on multi-threaded capacity rather than peak single-core throughput. Fitting workloads include web servers, enterprise backend services, database operations, software build systems, and microservice container deployment.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6a.4xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine equipped with 16 vCPUs (8 physical cores) powered by an AMD EPYC 7H12 processor at 2.6 GHz and 64 GB of memory. It operates on x86_64 architecture under KVM virtualization without local ephemeral storage or GPU acceleration, providing a 5 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark evaluations reflect average multi-core and application handling capabilities, evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 7328, PassMark CPU score of 19093.04, and Redis SET throughput of 14.17 million operations per second. However, single-core processing and uncached memory bandwidth show performance constraints. The balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory configuration delivers qualitative cost efficiency for standard operational environments, making it suitable for web serving, microservices, software compilation, and general enterprise application hosting.
